title: Paper-clay wreath wall decoration
subtitle: A circular wreath of moulded leaves and flowers, built from paper clay
excerpt: A decorative wall wreath made from individual leaves and flowers pressed and modelled in paper-clay air-dry clay, then assembled on a wire ring armature. The cellulose fibres in paper clay keep thin petal and leaf shapes from cracking during drying, making it better suited to this kind of detailed work than plain air-dry clay.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Paper clay properties referenced from standard craft literature; no specific copyright source reproduced.

glossaryTerms.definition: Air-dry clay mixed with cellulose paper fibres that strengthen thin sections and improve joint strength
The drying stage where clay holds its shape but is still damp enough to join pieces without cracking
Clay thinned with water to a paste consistency and used as an adhesive between clay pieces
Fully air-dried and unfired; the clay is stable but fragile before sealing

content.text: A clay wreath is built element by element: a batch of leaves, a few flower heads, some small berries or seed pods, all made from
paper clay

to resist cracking in the thin sections. Each element dries separately, then they are joined onto a wire ring with slip and allowed to dry together. No kiln is required. The finished wreath can be painted in any season's palette.

materials.name: Clay slip (same paper clay thinned with water)
Wire ring frame, 25 cm diameter (craft wire or a wire coat hanger bent to a circle)
Acrylic paints (green, white, ochre, or seasonal tones)

content.text: Making the elements
Make all elements before assembling. Allow them to reach
leather-hard
before joining to the frame. A full wreath needs roughly 20 to 30 leaves and 5 to 8 flower or bud elements.
Leaves
Flatten a small piece of paper clay to about 3 mm thick. Cut a leaf shape roughly 5 to 7 cm long and 3 cm wide with a fettling knife. Pinch the tip to a point.
Press a central vein into each leaf using the needle tool. Add 3 to 5 side veins radiating outward from the central vein.
Curl the leaf slightly by draping it over a cylinder (a pen, a thin dowel) and leaving it to dry in that position for 20 minutes, then set it flat. This gives a slight natural curve.
Flowers
Roll a small ball of clay about 2 cm in diameter. Press it flat with a thumb to form a disc roughly 4 cm across and 4 mm thick.
Using the needle tool or fettling knife, score 5 petal divisions around the circumference. Each petal should extend to within 5 mm of the disc edge. Thin the outer edge of each petal by pinching.
Add small balls of clay to the centre of each flower to form stamens. Press a needle tool tip into each ball to texture it.
Assembling the wreath
Score the back of each leaf and flower. Apply
slip
to the scored area. Press each element against the wire ring, overlapping leaves at a consistent angle so they face slightly outward.
Place flowers at intervals between leaf clusters. Press firmly and allow the slip to grip for a minute before continuing around the ring.
Fill any gaps with small oval berries rolled from clay, slipped, and pressed in between elements.
Drying
Lay the assembled wreath flat on a board and allow it to reach
bone-dry
over two to three days. Do not hang the wreath to dry while wet as the weight of wet clay will pull the lower elements off the wire frame.
Finishing

Apply two coats of PVA to all clay surfaces. Once dry, paint with acrylics: greens and ochres for a botanical look, white and gold for a winter wreath, dusty pinks and sage for spring. Seal with a final matte varnish coat.
Use and care
Hang indoors away from humidity. Wipe with a dry cloth only. Paper clay is more durable than plain air-dry but is still not waterproof.
Variations
Make a half-wreath and mount it to a wooden panel for a flatter wall piece with a smaller profile.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Leaves detach from the wire frame during drying
items.cause: The back of the leaf was not scored before slipping, reducing adhesion to the wire
items.fix: Reattach with fresh slip on a re-scored surface. Paper clay adhesion across a wire is reinforced by pressing a thin coil of fresh clay over the joint on the back

items.problem: Petal tips on the flowers crack off
items.cause: Very thin pinched tips dried faster than the rest of the flower
items.fix: Reattach with slip. For the next batch, keep petal tips at least 2 mm thick and allow to dry slowly under a damp cloth

items.problem: Whole sections of the wreath sag downward after hanging
items.cause: The wreath was hung before fully bone-dry
items.fix: Always allow full bone-dry drying flat before hanging. Once sealed with PVA the assembly is stable
